category_title: Students with ASD exhibiting inappropriate physical contact and out-of-seat behavior
minimal_context: Matthew is transitioning from a reinforcing activity back to his desk for a formal teaching session in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Matthew, you have finished accessing your reinforcing activity. Please return to your seat for our teaching time.

STUDENT: (Stands up from the activity area but does not return to his seat, walking to another part of the classroom instead.)

TUTOR: Matthew, it is time to sit at your desk.

STUDENT: (Continues to wander around the room, demonstrating out-of-seat behavior during the scheduled teaching time.)

TUTOR: Please come back to your seat so we can begin.

STUDENT: (Leaves the teaching area completely without permission, continuing his out-of-seat behavior which disrupts the session.)

options.A: Implement a behavior contract where the student earns home computer access when criteria are met, and provide a surprise school reward for earning five green stickers in a week.
options.B: Guide the student to progressively tune their awareness to each body part, followed by intentionally relaxing each part of the body from their toes to the top of their heads.
options.C: Use applications like Look2Learn and Stories2Learn to create personalized stories with recorded photos and audio to prepare the student for transitioning back to the desk for formal teaching time.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task during the daily teaching sessions, ensuring the student understands when the reinforcing activity concludes and formal teaching begins.
